howItWorks.intro: Blueprint & Build is how the practice does Asset Based Consulting: every two months we turn one idea into a reusable asset. Ideas are always open. Each cycle opens with a 10-day vote, then the winner is blueprinted with the person who sent it, and two builders ship it in the time that is left.

steps.title: Share an idea, any time
steps.summary: The idea form is always open. Every idea joins a backlog, and the best ones are brought into the next cycle.
steps.detail: Use the brief builder: your idea in one line, the problem and who has it, up to three things the MVP does, a ten-minute demo, the data and what is out of scope. No GitHub account or login is needed. There is no cut-off, so an idea sent today waits in the backlog for the next shortlist.

steps.title: Triage the backlog
steps.summary: Before each vote opens, the two builders score the backlog in one short session.
steps.detail: Each idea is scored from 1 to 5 on impact, feasibility, reusability and showcase value, with impact and feasibility counting double. The data check is pass or fail: only internal, public or synthetic data gets through. The top three become the shortlist, and the rest stay in the backlog.

steps.title: Vote for 10 days
steps.summary: The practice picks the winner from the shortlist of three with a reaction emoji in Slack.
steps.detail: Voting stays open for 10 working days in the Slack channel, with one reminder and a mention on the practice call. The idea with the most reactions wins, and ties go to the higher feasibility score. Runners-up stay in the backlog and are shortlisted again automatically next cycle, once. Results and turnout are published on this site.

steps.title: Blueprint with the owner
steps.summary: The winning idea is scoped with the person who suggested it, in the week after the vote.
steps.detail: The builders and the idea owner agree what a demoable slice looks like, and anything that does not fit is logged as v2. The aim is something two builders can finish in about 6 person-days.

steps.title: Build it
steps.summary: Two builders build the winner across the rest of the two-month cycle.
steps.detail: The build takes about 6 person-days, shared by the two builders. The idea owner is invited to test it first, and anything unfinished is cut back to a slice that can be demoed. The builders also write down what they learn, so it is shared through Knowledge Share.

steps.title: Ship and MVP Drop
steps.summary: The MVP ships with docs and a demo, then is played back live to the practice.
steps.detail: In the last week the builders test it, write the README and record a demo. On the last working day of the cycle it is played back in a 20-minute MVP Drop, then added to the catalog as Live, and the next cycle starts with its own vote.

rules.title: About 6 person-days
rules.text: An MVP has to be buildable in about 6 person-days, shared by two builders across the build stage of a cycle.

rules.title: Demoable in 10 minutes
rules.text: If it cannot be shown working in 10 minutes, it is too big or too vague for one cycle.

rules.title: No client data
rules.text: Internal, public or synthetic data only. Ideas that need client data do not pass the data check at triage.

rules.title: Approved tools only
rules.text: MVPs use approved tools and AI services only.

rules.title: Shipped as is
rules.text: Every MVP is documented and has an owner, but comes with no support commitment. Feedback goes to the Slack channel.

rules.title: Bigger ideas wait
rules.text: Anything bigger goes to a Productionise shortlist (a longer-term list for bigger ideas that deserve proper investment), not the build stage.

faq.q: What counts as an MVP here?
faq.a: A small working tool that two builders can make in about 6 person-days and demo in 10 minutes. It can be a script, a tool hosted on an internal platform, a spreadsheet or Power BI file, or a Claude skill.

Building something reusable once, so every engagement can start from it instead of from a blank page. Each MVP is an asset: a skill, a dashboard or a template that the practice can take into client work, as long as it was built on internal, public or synthetic data.

Passing on what we learn. Every MVP ships with a short guide, and the builders share the lessons from each cycle with the practice. The Hall of fame links to a Box folder where the MVPs and their documents are kept.
Anyone in the practice, at any time. The form is always open and your idea joins the backlog. Your name is optional, but giving it means the idea owner gets the credit.

Every two months, on the first Monday of January, March, May, July, September and November (the next working day if that Monday is a bank holiday). The vote runs for 10 working days, the Blueprint with the idea owner takes the next 5, and the build fills the rest of the two months. The Vote page shows the dates for the current cycle.

faq.q: Do I need a GitHub account?
faq.a: No. Ideas go in through the form on this site, you vote with a reaction in Slack, and every download in the catalog is a single zip file.

faq.q: What happens to ideas that don't win?
faq.a: Runners-up stay in the backlog and are shortlisted again automatically in the next cycle, once. The best idea that did not win can also get an idea of the cycle shout-out.
Internal, public or synthetic data only. Never client data. The data check at triage is pass or fail, so an idea that needs client data cannot reach the shortlist.
No. MVPs are shipped as is: documented and owned, but with no support commitment. Send feedback to the Slack channel. Each MVP is reviewed every 6 months and retired if nobody uses it.

faq.q: How do I install a Claude skill?
faq.a: Download the skill's zip from the Claude Skills page and upload it in the Claude app, or use Copy for Claude Code to paste the skill straight into Claude Code. The How to install panel on that page has the steps.
Yes, ask in the Slack channel. The aim is for one volunteer to join each cycle as a guest builder, to learn alongside the two regular builders.

points: Voting stays open for 10 working days, with one reminder in the channel and a mention on the practice call.
You vote with a reaction emoji on the idea you want, in the Slack channel. No login beyond Slack.
The idea with the most reactions wins.
Ties go to the idea with the higher feasibility score from triage.
Runners-up stay in the backlog and are shortlisted again automatically next cycle, once.
Results and turnout are published on this site.

install.intro: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file that teaches Claude a repeatable task. Use whichever of these fits how you work.

steps.title: Claude app
steps.text: Download the zip from the skill's card. In Claude, go to Customize > Skills and choose Upload a skill, then pick the zip. Skills you upload are private to you.

steps.title: Claude Code: copy and paste
steps.text: Press Copy for Claude Code on the skill's card, then paste into Claude Code. It contains the whole skill and asks Claude Code to save it in ~/.claude/skills/, so it works in every project. Nothing to download or unzip.

steps.title: Claude Code: from the zip
steps.text: Unzip the download. The unzipped folder that contains SKILL.md is the skill folder (skill-folder in the commands below). Copy it into ~/.claude/skills/ to use it in every project, or into .claude/skills/ inside one repo (run those two commands from that repo's folder) to use it there only.
steps.code:
# for all your projects
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -r skill-folder ~/.claude/skills/

# for one repo only
mkdir -p .claude/skills
cp -r skill-folder .claude/skills/
